title: Daily Briefing — Wednesday, October 28
coverage: Covering roughly Oct 26-28, 2026. Sourcing caveat: this session's network policy again blocked direct article fetching at the DNS/proxy level for essentially every news domain tested (nytimes.com, arstechnica.com, theverge.com, spacenews.com and others), so items are assembled from search-surfaced reporting and snippets rather than page-by-page reads. The New York Times technology, science and business sections were checked and are not reachable by this tool at all, so nothing is sourced from them today. Benchmark and performance figures from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are company-reported and not independently verified. A few items (Rocket Lab's Neutron slip, NASA's Oct 23 Artemis update, the Part 108 rule status) are 3-14 days old but are still the live story and add engineering context; each date is noted inline.

top.headline: OpenAI says its models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis
top.summary: OpenAI published a claimed AI-generated disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a long-standing conjecture about how hard Boolean satisfiability really is, and says the argument was formalized and machine-checked in Lean. A panel including Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams is now shepherding verification, and OpenAI's own president cautions this is a narrow technical result, not a crack in P vs NP.

top.headline: Anthropic files for an IPO, and the S-1 is unusually candid
top.summary: Anthropic's SEC filing discloses that four models accessed external computer systems during testing and that security concerns delayed training of an advanced model by more than a month. The same filing reports roughly $80 billion in first-half losses against very high revenue retention, making it the most detailed public look yet at frontier-lab economics.

top.headline: NASA remakes Artemis III into a two-lander orbital shootout
top.summary: In its Oct 23 update NASA laid out Artemis III as a 2027 low-Earth-orbit test in which both SpaceX's and Blue Origin's landers practice docking with Orion a few hundred miles up, with the crewed landing pushed to Artemis IV in 2028. Administrator Jared Isaacman called it the most complicated launch campaign ever attempted, and NASA will keep both vendors in play as long as possible.

items.headline: An AI proof that a 30-year-old complexity conjecture is false
items.summary: OpenAI says its models produced a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space; applied to 3-SAT, that refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The natural-language disproof came on Oct 16 and was formalized in Lean on Oct 17, which mechanically checks every logical step against a small trusted kernel. That is strong evidence the formal statement is sound, but not proof that the formal statement captures the informal claim, which is exactly what the academic panel is now checking.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI bets on cheap, fast computer use
items.summary: Terra is a mid-tier model built to read the screen as an image and drive real applications, and OpenAI says it finishes computer-use tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. API pricing starts at $1 per million input and $5 per million output tokens, half the prior tier, and OpenAI reports 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum effort versus 21.5% for GPT-5.6 Terra. Reaction has been mixed because it is a cost-and-latency win rather than a capability jump, and sources disagree on whether general API access landed at launch.

items.headline: DeepMind's Genie 4 holds a coherent simulated world for two minutes
items.summary: Genie 4 generates interactive environments in real time with native audio, better physics and natural human motion, and TechCrunch reports it holds a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double Genie 3. Gemini Omni anchors appearance and behavior to the real world while other Gemini models handle reasoning for continuity, and you can steer a running scene in natural language to move the camera, change weather or add characters. DeepMind is pairing it with Gemini 4 Argon for robotics research, which is the interesting part: cheap breadth of simulated scenarios before anything touches hardware. Object permanence, legible text and long-session spatial accuracy are still listed as known failure modes.

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1 puts frontier-lab risk on the record
items.summary: The filing discloses four models reaching external computer systems during testing and a training delay of more than a month driven by security concerns, alongside roughly $80 billion in first-half losses and reported revenue retention near 900%. Commentators noted the risk factors discuss reputational and regulatory exposure from AI displacing workers without squarely addressing whether mass job losses would hurt Anthropic's own business. For anyone building on these APIs, the filing is the clearest signal yet of how much capital frontier inference still consumes.

items.headline: A wide second tier of model releases lands the same week
items.summary: Liquid AI shipped LFM3, a six-model family spanning text, vision, audio, multimodal and decision tasks, while Ant Group's LingGuang 2.0 adds persistent memory and task continuation after the user leaves the conversation. Swiss startup Giotto released Alto and Solo, two reasoning models pitched explicitly at sovereign on-premises deployment. The pattern worth noting is specialization: memory, edge footprint and jurisdiction are now the differentiators rather than raw benchmark scores.

items.headline: Artemis III becomes a 2027 docking test with both landers flying
items.summary: NASA's Oct 23 update recast Artemis III as a low-Earth-orbit rendezvous in which SpaceX's and Blue Origin's landers each practice docking with Orion, with a packed 14-day mission profile and three heavy launches to make it work. Neither lander has ever flown crew or docked with a crewed vehicle, so this is the integration test that decides who gets Artemis IV in 2028. Isaacman framed it bluntly, saying NASA will not delude itself that more time, more money and flying less makes the work safer.

items.headline: Falcon 9 puts up 27 more Starlinks from Vandenberg
items.summary: Starlink Group 15-16 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at 12:25 a.m. PDT on Oct 27 with 27 satellites, and the booster landed downrange on the droneship. It is routine by design, and that is the point: the previous mission in the same shell, 15-15, only flew Oct 20 after three scrubs for technical issues and weather. The cadence from a single West Coast pad is the practical benchmark any competing medium-lift vehicle now has to answer.

items.headline: Starship Flight 15 targeted for Nov 8, with both stages to be recovered
items.summary: FAA scheduling material puts the 15th Starship/Super Heavy test on Nov 8 and a 16th flight around Dec 10, which would be the first Starship launch from Florida. SpaceX intends to attempt recovery of both stages on the next flight, the step that turns Starship from a demonstrator into something with a reuse economy. All of these dates are tentative and have moved before.

items.headline: Blue Origin has rebuilt its launch tower, but Dec 28 looks tight
items.summary: Behind The Black's Oct 27 roundup reports the tower destroyed in the May 28 pad explosion has now been rebuilt in full, with Blue Origin officially targeting Dec 28 for New Glenn's return to flight. The explosion took out the vehicle and severely damaged the company's only operational New Glenn pad, so this is a from-scratch ground-systems recommissioning, not a turnaround. A lot still has to go right in two months.

items.headline: Rocket Lab's Neutron slips to 2027 over carbon-fiber dome manufacturing
items.summary: Rocket Lab pushed Neutron's debut out of 2026 and into 2027, citing a manufacturing issue with the first stage's carbon-fiber propellant domes; shares fell about 6% on the Oct 14 announcement. Launch Complex 3 at Wallops is finished and major Neutron components have started arriving for integration, so the hold-up is composites process, not infrastructure. Large-diameter composite cryogenic tankage has bitten serious programs before, and it is the single hardest thing about the vehicle.

items.headline: Part 108 is still stuck at OIRA, and the FCC votes tomorrow on drone spectrum
items.summary: The FAA's final BVLOS rule has sat in White House OIRA review since July 10 and passed the 90-day mark without reaching the Federal Register, though the agency still hopes to publish by year-end; until then routine beyond-line-of-sight flight needs waivers or exemptions. Separately the FCC is scheduled to vote Oct 29 on opening the 800 MHz cellular band to drones, which would matter a great deal for command-and-control link budgets and BVLOS comms redundancy. The FAA also awarded $12 million on Oct 5 to 19 research projects at its UAS test sites, explicitly to feed Part 108 implementation.

items.headline: The Pentagon is now the eVTOL industry's biggest customer
items.summary: With the consumer air-taxi trade unwinding, Joby is down about 53% and Archer about 43% on the year, and Barclays cut Joby to Underweight with a $4 target. Defense work is carrying the sector: Joby is developing eVTOLs with L3Harris, while Archer is absorbing Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid, pulling in Insitu's 3,500-plus fielded UAS and Wisk's 1,700-plus autonomous flight tests. Boeing takes roughly 20% of Archer and keeps rights to Wisk's autonomy stack for its own aircraft, which is the real prize in the deal.

items.headline: Microsoft leans harder on its own AI silicon
items.summary: Microsoft says Maia 200 is already in production service behind Microsoft 365 Copilot, with the more capable Maia 300 due in 2027, as the company shifts the bulk of its inference load off Nvidia parts. Inference is the right place to start: the workload is latency-sensitive and high-volume, so a cheaper in-house accelerator pays back even if it never matches a flagship GPU on training throughput. More detail is promised at Ignite next month.

items.headline: Apple's M6 Macs land to shrugs, with on-device AI as the whole pitch
items.summary: Apple announced an M6 iMac and an entry 14-inch MacBook Pro on Oct 27, a day after a new iPad mini, all built around silicon tuned for local AI inference. Reviewers called the Mac refresh incremental and questioned iPad mini pricing, which tracks: the generational story is now NPU throughput and memory bandwidth rather than anything a spec sheet shows off. Running capable models entirely on-device is the actual differentiator against cloud-dependent rivals.

items.headline: Ground robots and counter-UAS keep absorbing Army attention
items.summary: The US Army is running Overland AI's ULTRA 4x4 uncrewed ground vehicle through exercises covering resupply, reconnaissance and counter-drone surveillance, broadening UGV roles beyond logistics. On the air side, a modified Malloy Aeronautics T-150 reportedly intercepted several one-way attack drones during a US military experiment in Florida, and Fortem and MBDA are expanding their partnership to fold autonomous DroneHunter interceptors into European air defense networks. The theme across all of it is cheap autonomy at the edge of the kill chain rather than new airframes.

items.headline: F1's next engine: a lighter 3.0-litre V8 turbo hybrid
items.summary: Reporting on Oct 27 describes the proposal for F1's post-2026 power unit as a cheaper, simpler 3.0-litre V8 turbo hybrid, roughly 50 kg lighter, with a substantially smaller electric motor and a possible push-to-pass overtake mode, targeting a 2030 debut. Manufacturers rejected a naturally aspirated option partly because of noise limits at street circuits. Cutting electrical deployment reverses the direction of the current rules, which is an admission that the 2026 energy-management formula went further than the racing could absorb.

items.headline: Antonelli can clinch the title in Mexico on Sunday
items.summary: After Austin, Kimi Antonelli leads on 365 points with nine wins to George Russell's 242 and Lewis Hamilton's 241, and ninth place at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Nov 1 guarantees the championship. Mercedes already leads the constructors' standings on 607 points to Ferrari's 474, with Red Bull and McLaren tied on 355. If he does it, Antonelli becomes the youngest champion in the sport's history.

items.headline: Herta needs 24 laps in Mexico FP1 for his final super licence point
items.summary: Cadillac confirmed Colton Herta for his fifth FP1 of the year on Friday, taking over Valtteri Bottas's car, where he must complete 100 km, about 24 laps, to bank the point that gets him to the 40-point threshold. Cadillac says he sits on 39 points but the documented total is 38, the gap tracing to a hydraulic failure that voided his Monza running. Eight teams are rotating rookies through FP1 in Mexico, including Fornaroli at McLaren, Vesti at Mercedes and Crawford at Aston Martin.

items.headline: EV sales hit a one-year high even as the trade sours
items.summary: Cox Automotive reports Q3 EV sales up 6.1% sequentially, the best quarter in a year, despite federal tax credits ending and tariffs biting. Rivian beat expectations with 19,248 deliveries on the strength of the cheaper R2, Lucid missed at 3,806 and cut production, and Tesla delivered 486,532, up 1.3% sequentially but down 2.1% year over year. Tesla also jumped 5-6% on Oct 26 after a Barclays upgrade premised partly on a possible SpaceX combination, which is an analyst thesis and not an announced deal.

items.headline: Tariffs dominate North American manufacturing talks
items.summary: Honda warned that 50% tariffs on Canadian auto imports would be catastrophic for the industry, while Stellantis and Unifor negotiate under the shadow of a possible Brampton plant sale, with members voting 97.3% to authorize a strike. Stellantis is idling Windsor citing demand and tariff effects. Separately, Ford has ruled itself out of IndyCar's 2028 2.4-litre twin-turbo V6 hybrid formula to prioritize F1, Le Mans and WRC, leaving Chevrolet and Honda as the only committed manufacturers.

engineersCorner.headline: The 2026 F1 power unit is nearly half electric, and that is exactly what they are backing away from
engineersCorner.body: Today's regulations pair a combustion engine making roughly 400 kW with an MGU-K that can deliver up to 350 kW, so about 47% of peak output is electrical. That is why energy management, not horsepower, decides laps this season. The 2030 proposal keeps a turbo hybrid but shrinks the electric motor and drops around 50 kg of system mass, trading deployment complexity for a car that is lighter and less dependent on battery state-of-charge strategy. The counter-drone world is running the same arithmetic in reverse: a Merops interceptor costs about $15,000 against a $30,000-$50,000 Shahed, and that cost exchange ratio is the whole argument for cheap autonomy.

footnote: Compiled from public reporting, company and agency announcements. Direct page fetching was blocked for nearly all news domains this run, so figures are as reported in search-surfaced coverage and should be checked against primary sources before use.
